text:
Buffalo played well enough to win this one for long stretches, and Adin Hill would not allow it. The Sabres outshot Vegas 15-6 in the first period, finished with 78 shot attempts to 51, and won even strength 3.13 expected goals to 1.83. Hill stopped 28 of 29 and saved 2.9 goals more than his shots deserved, and the Golden Knights left with a 4-1 win and their third straight.

The first period was all Buffalo, 1.71 expected goals to 0.49, with Tage Thompson and Zach Benson both stopped by Hill in the final seconds. Then Vegas scored the way teams do when they've been on their heels: Mitch Marner, alone, shorthanded, on a 63% chance at 12:17 of the second. Jack Eichel, the former Sabres captain, added another 86 seconds later and, as Matthew Fairburn of The Athletic noted, skated to the glass and raised his arms at the crowd. You can decide for yourself how that played in Buffalo.

The Sabres did get one back early in the third, a goal-mouth scramble finally credited to Beck Malenstyn, and their win chance climbed from 9% to 25%. Tomas Hertl took it back 77 seconds later off a Marner pass, then made it 4-1 on an Ivan Barbashev feed at 10:00. Both power plays went 0 for 3. The Sabres' own video of Thompson's postgame carried the line "We were chasing the game at that point," which is the second half of this game in a sentence.

By the full count of chances, Buffalo deserved to win 51% of the time. That's the frustrating part for the Sabres: they did most of what you'd ask and lost by three. For Vegas, a road trip that included Trevor Connelly's late winner in Detroit keeps rolling, and Hill now has a game to point to in the crease conversation with Carter Hart.
headline: Adin Hill steals one in Buffalo
